A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transform-neck and surrogate-loss image-compression framework despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original rate-accuracy experiments, reconstruction-quality measurements, complexity comparisons, ablations, and qualitative results, including the appendix VVC comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds visual-encoder generalization tests, additional benchmark results, and token-level feature-error analysis.

M1.justification: The architecture and loss ingredients remain; progressive cross-entropy/distillation training already appeared in v1 Appendix A.1. However, the stated d2/d3 training sequence changes: v1 Section 3.5 specifies a final frozen-codec neck fine-tune after joint optimization, whereas v2's two-phase procedure ends with joint optimization. This establishes a revised stated recipe, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds MMBench and POPE evaluations in Section 4.6 and Appendix A.5. This extends benchmark coverage within image-language tasks while retaining ImageNet, COCO captioning, SEED-Bench, RefCOCO, and Kodak.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain Reconstruction, U-Net Post-processing, and VVC/VTM comparisons, including the existing ELIC/TIC codec comparison. The added benchmarks use existing Reconstruction and uncompressed references. Token-reduction methods are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 substantially broadens the evaluation design beyond shared CLIP ViT encoders: Section 4.6 tests mPLUG-Owl2's custom ViT and Osprey's CLIP ConvNeXt encoder. Appendix A.5 evaluates Honeybee and Shikra on the same POPE benchmark, and Figure 7 introduces an equal-training-step feature-error comparison. Original splits, rate settings, and the 5,000-group few-shot protocol remain.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 compares spatial token-MSE reductions from cross-entropy, distillation, and progressive training using two image examples. This adds a focused diagnostic to the retained layer-removal, loss-function, and codec ablations. Existing qualitative appendix examples are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The retained randomly sampled few-shot evaluation groups do not constitute newly added repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 8 and 10 add substantial result sets for mPLUG-Owl2 on MMBench and Osprey, Honeybee, and Shikra on POPE, generally showing better rate-accuracy tradeoffs than Reconstruction. Figure 7 adds feature-error outcomes. These are new experimental results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings; the original ablation, VVC, complexity, and qualitative results are retained.

T1.justification: V2's cosine-similarity, cross-entropy, and piecewise curriculum equations formalize procedures already described in v1 Section 3.4 and Appendix A.1. They add explicit notation rather than new mathematical reasoning. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central applicability claim expands from universality among MLLMs sharing the CLIP visual encoder to a framework applicable across visual-encoder architectures. V2 distinguishes retraining for different encoders from reuse without retraining among models sharing an encoder. The first-study claim and three application scenarios remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that cross-entropy emphasizes foreground feature alignment while distillation reduces global errors, and explains how token reduction could complement transmission compression. It also revises the earlier custom-encoder limitation through retrained generalization examples. The human/machine quality tradeoff and image-only scope remain.

D1.justification: V2 retains optimizer settings, RTX 4090 training time, model specifications, and asset-access information, and explicitly states 24 GB GPU memory. However, it omits v1 Appendix A.1's learning rates of 10^-4 and 10^-5 and the 20-epoch duration of the final distillation-only curriculum stage. The earlier curriculum's loss ratio and transition epochs are relocated into Section 3.5.

R1.justification: V2 adds CrossGet, TokenPacker, Osprey, and POPE references, discusses complementarity with token reduction, and emphasizes the cross-entropy term's distinction from earlier compression methods. It trims several earlier MLLM citations. The mPLUG-Owl2 reference is retained with updated publication information, rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central method exposition are substantially rewritten around general visual encoders and explicit training phases. The curriculum moves from the appendix into the main explanation, the ablation discussion is reordered, and new generalization and discussion sections are integrated. The title, affiliations, and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds feature-error heatmaps, generalization plots, additional POPE plots, and a system-cost diagram in Figures 7, 8, 10, and 11. Table 1 gains separate training-phase columns, Table 2 drops its metric column, and architecture diagrams and plot layouts are revised. Existing VVC and qualitative figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence beyond shared CLIP encoders and adds a useful diagnostic of the training losses, while making the training exposition clearer. These gains are partly offset by omitted learning rates and training-duration details, which weaken reproducibility. With the original framework and central findings largely retained, the net quality improvement is limited but supported.
